 Judgment
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.1967/2016 dated 27.06.2018 on the file of VIII Addl. SCJ & XXXIII, ACMM & MACT, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.11,50,000/- and the Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.50,000/-.

An application is filed under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC by the learned counsel for the Appellant stating that the medical bills for an amount of Smt C A Sumalatha vs Sri Nagaraju on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7543264/
2 Rs.58,275/- could not be filed before the court below.

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel for the Appellant submits that if the matter is remanded back to the court below,
they will examine the doctor in support of the medical bills.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that when these bills are very much available with the claimant and why he has not filed those documents NC: 2023:KHC:41972 before the court below is not known and there is no explanation forth coming in this regard.
In this regard, it is submitted that after these many years, remanding the matter would not serve the purpose.
5. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.

It is stated in support of the additional evidence application that he has produced voluminous medical records before the Tribunal, but the same were not properly marked and same were not considered by the Tribunal, as such he has come up with this appeal.

Considering these bills which amounts to Rs.50,000/- and odd, in the interest of both the parties this court deems it appropriate to remand the matter giving an opportunity to the claimant to examine the doctor in support of the same, the insurance company will also be at liberty to cross-examine the doctor.

Only to this limited extent,
the matter is remanded back to the court below.

Accordingly the award passed by the MACT dated 27.06.2018 is set aside and the matter is remanded back for consideration on the additional medical bills which are filed along with the petition under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC, further to examine the doctor and to cross-examine the same.
Without further notice, both the parties shall appear before the MACT on 15.12.2023 and within three months from 15.12.2023 the Tribunal shall dispose off the matter.
(i) Without further notice, both the parties shall appear before the MACT on 15.12.2023 and within three months from 15.12.2023 the Tribunal shall dispose off the matter.
(ii) The Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Record to the Tribunal along with the certified copy of the order passed by this court forthwith without any delay.
NC: 2023:KHC:41972 (iii) Application filed by the Appellant under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC shall be sent to the Tribunal along with this order copy.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
